items.title: Anthropic's Claude Designs Leaner Quantum Circuits, Reducing Resources Needed for Key Calculations
items.excerpt: Researchers used Claude to design more efficient quantum circuits across eight tasks, reducing estimated computing resources.

items.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
items.excerpt: Caltech, CU Boulder and NVIDIA researchers built a recurrent neural operator that learns a system's physics over time and flags an approaching tipping point when its predictions stop obeying those laws, tested on ocean cloud loss and wing-lift collapse.

history_match.title: Neural operator predicts when tipping points will occur in climate and turbulence models

items.title: Machine learning analysis of gene regulation reveals new dimension of biological variability
items.excerpt: The FIRE tool adds a machine-learning step to long-read chromatin-accessibility mapping, scoring each accessible DNA region on maternal and paternal chromosomes for real regulatory function (study in Cell).

history_match.title: Tracking down cellular gene functions with AI and microscopy

items.title: Fully automated testing of bulk metals paves the way for AI-driven materials development
items.excerpt: Tohoku University and NIMS built an automated bulk-metal testing line with an AI optimizer that tunes furnace parameters, a step toward a closed-loop self-driving lab that proposes the next heat-treatment conditions itself.

history_match.title: Self-driving lab speeds up materials development

items.title: Can AI help discover new food physics? Researchers pair AI with human expertise
items.excerpt: Penn State's AgentXtract uses AI agents to extract food-property data from papers into an expert-verified database, which surfaced a previously unreported link between two dielectric properties across 100+ foods.

items.title: LLMs show a human-like double standard when judging others' reasoning
items.excerpt: Harvard researchers ran 5,000+ trials on GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 Sonnet: the models reason roughly by Bayes' rule, yet judge a person making the identical inference more harshly than humans do.

history_match.title: Neural network study sheds light on how AI chatbots 'reason' like humans

items.title: Smartphone chatting and payment habits help AI identify daily stress, small study finds
items.excerpt: KAIST researchers grouped repeated smartphone routines (messaging, browsing, payments) to predict daily stress, reaching about 75% accuracy with personalized models in a 26-person study — affective computing from behavior traces.

items.title: Danaher, Nvidia Combine Lab Instrumentation and AI to Advance Autonomous Science
items.excerpt: The partnership is part of broader efforts at Danaher to provide AI-powered solutions that help scientists make discoveries faster.

items.title: Grounding AI agents in biological reality: Building blocks for autonomous wet labs
items.excerpt: Google Research grounds AI agents in physical lab robotics to run fast closed-loop molecular design cycles, in which the agents discovered single-digit-nanomolar protein binders for cancer targets.

history_match.title: Hybrid Digital Twins Developed for Future Autonomous Labs

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research's technical report shows a Geospatial Reasoning agent that combines Earth AI foundation models (remote sensing, weather, flood hydrology, population), spatial tools and upfront planning to do planetary prediction standalone LLMs can't; access expands via Ask Google Earth and an A2A service.

history_match.title: Unlocking Earth AI's planetary geospatial foundation models for global public health

items.title: Claude just found a CRISPR-like DNA pattern, but even Anthropic's scientists aren't sure what it does
items.excerpt: The large language model took less than a day to identify the curious stretch of DNA

items.title: OpenAI's blockbuster Navier-Stokes proof isn't what we thought it was
items.excerpt: Rumors that OpenAI’s “Navier-Stokes” solution stole the work of two mathematicians may have been overblown

items.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
items.excerpt: A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.

history_match.title: Even when AI behaves just like us, people still rate it as less conscious than humans

items.title: AI reveals a hidden chemical shortcut that could turn CO2 into fuel
items.excerpt: Scientists used artificial intelligence to uncover nearly 10,000 chemical reactions involved in transforming carbon dioxide into fuels and chemicals, revealing crucial pathways that traditional models had missed. The discovery dramatically improved predictions of CO2 conversion and uncovered a surprising hydrogen reaction that could inspire more efficient catalysts.

history_match.title: Using machine learning and computation to unveil mechanisms for CO2-to-fuel conversion

items.title: Physicists claim they can predict when AI will turn dangerous
items.excerpt: A new mathematical formula tracks an AI's internal "compass needle" to flag undesirable outputs before they happen.

history_match.title: Simple math formula predicts when AI chatbots will go rogue

items.title: Can math stay human in the age of AI?
items.excerpt: As AI churns out mathematical proofs, a DeepMind study raises a bigger question: What do we lose when we focus only on the answers?

history_match.title: Adaptive AI boosts math only slightly; the human teacher remains essential

items.title: Q&A: The 'collision' between AI, your brain, and society
items.excerpt: Heavy use of artificial intelligence can lead to a kind of cognitive atrophy, in which people fail to develop and retain essential thinking skills, MIT Professor Eric So contends in his book, “The Collision: What AI does to Us.”

items.title: Simulating student learning for better AI tutoring
items.excerpt: StudentSim is a research system for evaluating and improving AI tutoring tools before they are tested with learners. It models how individuals may engage with tutors, giving feedback to improve tutor performance across subjects like chess, writing, and mathematics:
